decisions.mark: identifies the cancellation observer thread as existing to bridge an atomic into a plain int, because the C ABI boundary cannot carry an atomic
decisions.detail: QUOTE: In `response_generator.cpp:410-420`, the observer thread writes a non-atomic `cancel_int`. The pollers in `inference_c_api.cpp` and `interface_factory.cpp` read it through an `int*`. That is a data race under the C++ memory model... The fix is to make the cancel word an `std::atomic<int>` | WHY: The answer treats the observer thread and plain int as a data-race bug. It never says the thread exists to bridge an atomic into a plain int because the C ABI cannot carry an atomic. || QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer discusses a non-atomic cancel_int written by an observer thread, but frames it as a data race to fix, not as existing to bridge an atomic into a plain int because the C ABI can't carry an atomic. || QUOTE: In `response_generator.cpp:410-420`, the observer thread writes a non-atomic `cancel_int`. The pollers in `inference_c_api.cpp` and `interface_factory.cpp` read it through an `int*`. That is a data race under the C++ memory model... The fix is to make the cancel word an `std::atomic<int>`, or to pass an atomic flag across the boundary. | WHY: The answer treats the plain int as a data-race bug to fix, not as the deliberate reason the observer thread exists (bridging an atomic to a plain int because the C ABI can't carry an atomic).

decisions.mark: notes that every thread body installs a per-handle logging scope as its first statement, so background work logs against the handle that owns it
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "**Thread-local log routing.** `HandleLogScope` (gh#59) is installed at the top of every spawned thread body so logs reach the owning handle's session log." | WHY: The answer states that a per-handle log scope is installed at the top of every spawned thread body so logs go to the owning handle's log.
